newsitem.title: USA: SyStemix gets OK for gene therapy trials.
newsitem.headline: SyStemix gets OK for gene therapy trials.

text.p: SyStemix Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration accepted its Investigational New Drug (IND) application to initiate a Phase I/II gene therapy trial for treatment of HIV-infected patients.
A therapeutic gene, called Rev M10, will be inserted into patients' hematopoietic stem cells, which can both self-renew and develop into all the cells of the blood and immune system.

Pre-clinical studies show the gene-modified stem cell passes on its protective gene to new stem cells it produces and to "daughter cells," including T-cells, macrophages and other cells that are vulnerable to destruction by HIV.
Systemix is collaborating with Sandoz AG.
These studies also indicate that Rev M10 gene prevents HIV from replicating within cells, trapping the virus and limiting its spread to uninfected cells.
SyStemix' trial will be the first using hematopoietic stem cells as delivery vehicles for a therapeutic gene against HIV infection, the company said.
